title: What is Node.js?
overview: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime environment that allows developers to execute JavaScript code outside the browser. It is mainly used for building fast and scalable backend applications.

example.title: Node.js Usage
example.content:
✔ Backend APIs
✔ Web Servers
✔ Real-time Applications
✔ Command Line Tools

title: Why Use Node.js?
overview: Node.js allows developers to use JavaScript for both frontend and backend development. Its non-blocking architecture makes it efficient for handling many requests.

example.title: Node.js Benefits
example.content:
✔ Single programming language
✔ High performance
✔ Large package ecosystem
✔ Real-time support

title: Node.js vs Browser JavaScript
overview: Browser JavaScript runs inside web browsers, while Node.js runs JavaScript on the server side with access to system resources.

example.title: Comparison
example.content:
Browser JS:
- DOM access
- Runs in browser

Node.js:
- Server-side execution
- File system access

title: Features of Node.js
overview: Node.js provides several features that make it suitable for modern backend development.

example.title: Node.js Features
example.content:
✔ Event-driven architecture
✔ Non-blocking I/O
✔ Fast execution
✔ Cross-platform support

title: Where Node.js is Used
overview: Node.js is commonly used for APIs, real-time applications, streaming services, and backend systems.

example.title: Real World Uses
example.content:
✔ Chat applications
✔ REST APIs
✔ Online games
✔ Streaming platforms

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what Node.js is, why it is used, how it differs from browser JavaScript, and where it is applied.

example.title: Quick Revision
